name: Kitchen Low Decel
execution: Goblet Squat Iso-Hold (3s, light DB) + Immediate 2-Step Lateral Shuffle to Two-Foot Stick (hold 2s)
swap: Bodyweight Squat Hold (3s) + Lateral Shuffle to Stick

manual.why: Dinking and blocking at the kitchen line means holding a low stance, then stopping hard.
manual.cue: Sit low, then slide two steps and freeze.

name: Pop-Up Smash
execution: Light DB Thruster (5 reps, moderate) + Immediate Band Pull-Apart Y-Hold (3s)
swap: Med Ball Squat-to-Overhead Throw + Band Pull-Apart

manual.why: Overheads and lob defense need leg-to-arm force transfer.
manual.cue: Drive up from your legs like you are hitting the overhead, then pull the band apart.

name: Deep Kitchen Reach
execution: Light DB Deficit Forward Lunge (3s lower, 2s hold at bottom) + Immediate Push-Back to Two-Foot Split-Step Hop
swap: Forward Lunge Hold (2s) + Push-Back to Split-Step

manual.why: Reaching for a low dink loads the front knee and hip in a long lunge.
manual.cue: Control going down, speed coming back.

name: Forearm Anti-Deflection
execution: Bottom-Up KB Hold (20s) + Wrist Pulses (15s small-range rapid flex/ext)
swap: DB Farmer's Hold + Band Wrist Pulses

manual.why: The paddle face must stay steady on contact.
manual.cue: Keep the bell upright without letting it wobble, then pulse your wrist fast and small.

name: NVZ Rapid-Fire Iso-Block
execution: Squat Iso-Hold facing Wall (30s) + Rapid Wall Tennis Ball Rebounds (Alternating Hands)
swap: Squat Hold + Partner Rapid Med-Ball Chest Passes

manual.why: The kitchen line demands a locked-in lower half to eliminate head movement.
manual.cue: We need your legs to be a concrete foundation so your hands can move like lightning.

name: NVZ Retreat & Smash
execution: Drop-Step Lunge to 3m Backward Shuffle + Goblet DB Jump Squat (light DB held throughout), Two-Foot Landing
swap: Backpedal 3m + Bodyweight Vertical Jump

manual.why: Defending a lob requires rapid reversal of momentum.
manual.cue: When the lob goes up, you can't just run backward. We're training you to drop-step, track, and explode upward.

name: NVZ Boundary Reach & Recoil
execution: Deep Cossack Squat (reaching outside base, 2s hold) + Band-Resisted Instant Recoil to Center (band anchored at hip height)
swap: Lateral DB Lunge + Explosive Push-Back

manual.why: Reaching for a wide dink requires massive eccentric adductor strength to brake.
manual.cue: If you get stretched wide, you have to hit the brakes and spring back to center instantly.

name: Concentric Overload
execution: Deficit Split Squat (Drop DBs at bottom) + Immediate Unweighted Vertical Jump
swap: Box Squat (Pause) + Jump Squat

manual.why: Dropping the weight removes the slow lowering phase and makes the drive purely concentric.
manual.cue: Let the weights drop, and explode up with nothing in your hands.

name: Calf-Achilles Reach Armor
execution: Single-Leg Eccentric Calf Lower off Step (4s, 6 reps) + Immediate Low Pogo Hops (10 hops, two-foot landing)
swap: Slow Single-Leg Calf Lower on Floor + Jump Rope

manual.why: Calf and Achilles strains happen when the muscle lengthens under load at the kitchen.
manual.cue: Lower slowly to build the brakes, then bounce quick to wake the springs.

name: Side-to-Side Redirect
execution: Lateral Skater Bound + 2s Single-Leg Stick + Immediate Reverse Bound Back (bodyweight)
swap: Lateral Lunge to Stick + Push-Back Hop

manual.why: Doubles play demands repeated lateral stops and reversals within a few steps.
manual.cue: Slide out, stop dead, then fire back. Stopping is the skill.

name: Ankle Roll Armor
execution: Single-Leg Reach Iso (3s, bodyweight) + Immediate Lateral Hop to Single-Leg Stick (2s)
swap: Single-Leg Stance Hold + Lateral Step to Stick

manual.why: Lateral ankle sprains are common on side-to-side court movement.
manual.cue: Train it to hold steady on one leg, then catch you on the landing.

name: Volley Block Anti-Rotation
execution: Split-Stance Band Pallof Hold (5s) + Immediate Step-and-Punch (same band)
swap: Cable Pallof Hold + Step-and-Punch

manual.why: Fast volleys need a trunk that resists twisting while the arms react.
manual.cue: Hold the band still, then punch out and snap back to a solid stance.

name: Kitchen Dink Lift & Cross
focus: Low-Stance Isometric to Contralateral Sling Drive
execution: Low-Pulley Squat Iso-Hold (3s, handle at hip) + Immediate Stand-Up with Low-to-High Cross-Body Pull to Opposite Shoulder (same cable)
swap: Band Anchored Low: Squat Hold (3s) + Stand-Up Low-to-High Band Lift

manual.why: The dink stance is a held low position; rising into a crossing reach loads the diagonal sling.
manual.cue: Sit low and hold. Then stand up and sweep the handle across your body.

name: Dink Reach & Reset
execution: Single-Leg RDL Reach (4s lower, bodyweight or light DB in opposite hand) + Immediate Step Back to Two-Foot Split-Step Hop
swap: Staggered-Stance RDL Hold (3s) + Step Back to Ready Stance

manual.why: A low dink is a forward lean on one leg with the other trailing for balance.
manual.cue: Reach long with your hips back, then step back and bounce.

name: Dink Arc Scoop
execution: Light Med Ball Low Squat Hold (3s, ball between knees) + Immediate Stand-Up into Underhand Scoop Throw to Wall (2 kg, soft arc)
swap: Bodyweight Squat Hold (3s) + Stand-Up Scoop Throw with Tennis Ball

manual.why: Third-shot drops and dinks are soft arcs driven by the legs, not the arm.
manual.cue: Your legs throw it and your hands just guide it.

name: Transition Zone Advance & Plant
focus: Forward Deceleration to Balanced Ready Stance
execution: 5m Forward Run + Split-Step Stick (two-foot, 2s, low stance) + Immediate 2-Step Lateral Shuffle
swap: 3-Step Forward Run to Split-Step Stick

manual.why: After the third shot, players advance to the kitchen and must stop balanced.
manual.cue: Run in, split-step, and own your balance.

name: Pop-Up Smash
execution: Light DB Thruster (5 reps, moderate) + Immediate Band Pull-Apart Y-Hold (3s)
swap: Bodyweight Thruster (squat to mid-depth jump, overhead arm drive, 5 reps) + Band Pull-Apart Y-Hold (3s)

manual.why: Supersedes id 26 because its swap was not a swap. It replaced the DB thruster with a med ball squat-to-overhead throw, which changes the movement pattern rather than substituting equipment for it, so an athlete with no dumbbells was not getting an equivalent drill. The new swap keeps the same intent (explosive leg-to-arm drive) and the same band pull-apart, using bodyweight and band only. Med Ball came out of equipment because it was named only by the old swap. No change to focus, execution, category, or role.
manual.cue: Drive up from your legs like you are hitting the overhead, then pull the band apart.

name: Concentric Overload
execution: Deficit Split Squat (Heavy DB) + Drive to Tall + Release DBs + Immediate Vertical Jump
swap: Deficit Split Squat (Pause, Bodyweight) + Vertical Jump

manual.why: Dropping the weight removes the slow lowering phase and makes the drive purely concentric. || TAG CLEANUP ONLY - the biomechanical problem is NOT fixed and is still queued. Dead 'Plate' and 'Barbell' tags removed: neither implement is named anywhere in the record. The barbell was the more dangerous of the two, because a barbell cannot be dropped mid-drill - the exact hazard id 59 was corrected for - and a coach scanning tags could reasonably have read it as loadable equipment for this drill. Box moves to swap_equipment since only the swap uses it. STILL OPEN: the execution drops the dumbbells at the bottom of a live complex and then jumps, which is the filter 2 issue raised in the audit. That needs a separate supersede. || FILTER 2 FIX, PLUS THE INVERSION FIX. Audit reasoning, as recorded on id 123: 'the execution drops the dumbbells at the bottom of a live complex and then jumps.' The old execution released the load from the bottom of a deficit split squat - the least stable point of the movement, on one leg, with the drop and the takeoff fused into a single unbroken transition. That is a clunk: the athlete is still decelerating through the eccentric when the load leaves their hands. The load now stays in the hands until the athlete is standing tall and stable on both feet, is released there, and only then does the jump fire. The drive to tall is the missing bridge that makes it a contrast rather than a release mid-repetition. Dumbbells are droppable, so the exit is safe. The swap also changes: it was Box Squat + Jump Squat, which is two implements and a fifth kind of movement, and it was one of the three inversion warnings. It is now the bodyweight version of the same drill, needing nothing, so swap_equipment is omitted and the inversion check passes outright.
manual.cue: Let the weights drop, and explode up with nothing in your hands.

name: NVZ Rapid-Fire Iso-Block

swap: Squat Hold + Partner Rapid Med-Ball Chest Passes

manual.why: MECHANICAL DATA FIX - NO COACHING CHANGE. This record had the same folding defect as ids 30, 51 and 60: ['Med Ball', 'Partner'] was used only in the swap text but was folded into `equipment` instead of `swap_equipment`. The tag was not dead - it genuinely names an implement this drill needs - so it never tripped the dead-tag warning; it just sat in the wrong field, where it made the primary look like it needed a scarce tool it does not use, and it hid the split from filter 3 review. Correct split: `equipment` ['Wall', 'Tennis Ball', 'Med Ball', 'Partner'] -> ['Wall', 'Tennis Ball'], `swap_equipment` None -> ['Med Ball', 'Partner']. Execution, swap, focus, loading and rest are unchanged - the movement is identical and only the tag fields differ. Checked against the inversion check before writing: the swap needs 1 implement against the primary's 2, and the swap's implement is common-tier, so it is not trading a scarce tool for a cheaper one. Filter 3 intent is unchanged and now legible: comparing the two lists shows the swap drops the scarce implement, which is what the folded version could not express.
manual.cue: We need your legs to be a concrete foundation so your hands can move like lightning.
